title: Chapter 540
paragraphs: Chapter 540
Episode 145. Omen (9)
In the Kinzelo Council.

Agzak, Zephyrin took a bite of the cookie. It looked similar to a Leetra cookie, but the taste… it was horrendously unspeakable. It seemed that torturing one's tongue with a poker would be a better choice.
'How did they manage to make such a horrific snack, ladies of Caligo.'
The Caligo sisters, who baked the cookies themselves, were at the side, eyes gleaming, waiting for the evaluation.
Zephyrin gave an awkward smile and a slight nod, which made the sisters leap with joy, as if it was a great honor.
"Of course! Our cookie defeated those guys' cookies, sis!"
"Thanks for... eating... so... deliciously... Grand Duke."

Not only did they leap with joy, they joined Bubare and started running around the conference room like it was a playground, even singing strange songs. Naturally, such behavior further aggravated the gloomy mood of the executives.
'Since those demons came, there hasn't been a quiet day in the Council…. We can't even say anything because of the Grand Duke.'
'Balakht must also dislike the sight of them. If I say something, he'd probably rip my mouth, right? He doesn’t even know I'm on his side!'

'Bubare and... the female Bubare... both... are so disgusting. The female Bubare sometimes has a funny side, but no. Damn it! What am I thinking? They both are intolerable. How can Bianca hang out with them?'
Balakht, Jo, and Bischel clicked their tongues internally, and Zephyrin stared blankly out the window.
"Lord Zephyrin."
Margiella approached Zephyrin, wheeling her wheelchair.
"Miss Margiella."

"What are you thinking so deeply about? You look as if you've caught a terminal illness. A sense of sorrow seems to seep from your eyes. Maybe, a lover hidden in the demon world…? Oh my, that's too romantic."
It was strange.
When Zephyrin was rational, she was polite and kind to everyone, but she was merciless to those who crossed the line.
Especially to demons or dragons, and even more so to those who weren't superior. At least the head or heir of a demon's dukedom had to be careful when teasing her. Excluding fools like Ainas.
But for some reason, Zephyrin had never felt offended by Margiella's jokes.
'Well, considering the existence bound to you, it's not so surprising.'
Zephyrin helped Margiella to stand and sit next to her.

"I don’t have a terminal illness, but there’s a similar part, in the sense that I keep thinking about something. It's not love but hatred... Anyway, I was thinking about the sad thing Miss Margiella mentioned last time."
-"Shall I tell you a fun story to cheer you up, Lord Zephyrin?"
-"What is it?"
-"Maybe soon, a sad event might happen to Jin Kyung, Lord Zephyrin."
-"A sad event...?"
"You were thinking about Jin Kyung."
"I didn't know that the sad story you mentioned, Margiella, was about that stone."
"Ah, are you upset because I didn't tell you in advance?"
"It would be a lie if I say no, but perhaps it's because my master who lies in me is coughing up blood and puking like a sick person has some thoughts."
"Hmm, but! It was you, Lord Zephyrin, who made the leader cough up blood."
When Margiella brought up that story, the other executives in the meeting room perked up their ears and looked around.
The recent health status of the leader was the biggest issue in Kinzelo. Problems kept occurring while he was getting better.

He used his power willingly during the attack on Geomhwang City last year, but the problems that followed, including the Black King's group incident, the Sota Desert, and the accident that happened during this visit to Tikan, were all Zephyrin's responsibility.
But no one dared to question or blame Zephyrin. The only punishment she received was when Bischel once asked her to spy on Zipfel.
'Oh, indeed, the sister of the deputy leader! She's scratching right where it itches! Hmm, Zephyrin wouldn't intimidate Margiella, would she?'
'Even if it's Margiella, if she speaks so bluntly... will it be okay? Just thinking about a few stories from the demon world that Bianca told me, Zephyrin has crazier tendencies than Belakt.'
'Margiella! Well done! No, why would you say that!'
Despite the worries of Belakt, Jo, and Bischel, Zephyrin obediently nodded.
"Yes, it's my fault. I tried to be as careful as possible, but as you know... Jin Runcandel. That devil-like man is hopeless, isn't he?"
"Of course, I know it well. He's not an ordinary person, right? Considering how he has been a headache for us..."
"I wouldn't feel relieved even if I killed him a hundred times."
"Of course, you're right! But I still hope that Jin Kyung will become one of us."
"I've seen a lot of people like him in my long life. They're the kind of people who never ally with those with different beliefs."
"You're speaking as if you approve of Jin Kyung."
Zephyrin didn't answer and turned his head towards the window.
"Our Kinzelo is always open, so there might be a chance someday. Though it seems like your patience and Belakt's patience might run out first."
"You're a little strange, Margiella."
"Haha, I hear that sometimes."
"Jin Runcandel, if we really wanted him to be on our side, we should have told him about the true nature of the stone and made sure he was minimally involved in this matter."
"I've thought about that too. But even if we had told him about the true nature of the stone beforehand, we wouldn't be able to stop the predetermined fate, right?"
Predetermined fate.
What Margiella meant by that was the death of Dante Hairan.

"Your friend is bound to die, and the white stone is a dangerous object that must never be approached. Jin Gyeong won't listen even if we tell him that, right? As you said, Jin Gyeong is that kind of person."
Following Margiella's words, Zephyrin nodded.
"Hehe, fools! They don't even know the stone is a bomb... Uh, uh!"
As Bubare tried to intervene, Bischel quickly covered his mouth to prevent his disgusting voice from upsetting Zephyrin further.
To Bischel, the white stone was something that Bubare shouldn't even dare to mention.

"... Anyway, I'll be more careful about using my master's power in the future. For now, let's enjoy some snacks (while the Caligo sisters were not looking, Zephyrin threw the cookies they made out the window) and watch the spectacle. I hope Jin Gyeong chooses the date for the negotiation rationally after the incident is over."
April 4th, 1800.

Everyone in Gyeomhwangseong stayed up all night with their eyes wide open. An enormous enemy that they could never handle was approaching Gyeomhwangseong, and the seal on the white stone that enveloped Dante was showing an even darker color of chaos than the day before.
The knights gathered in Gyeomhwangseong still showed no signs of leaving Dante.

It wasn't because they believed in the power of the Vamel Alliance. It wasn't because they gained hope from their great victory in the first battle. And it wasn't because they believed Jin could perform that miraculous divine power again.
The knights knew very well that they couldn't do anything on their own and with the Vamel Alliance when Zipfel's true forces arrived.
The reason the Hairan knights didn't leave was due to loyalty, faith, and efficiency.
"If anyone should leave, it should be Jin Gyeong, not us."
Shuras Helter said. He looked pale from the internal injuries he sustained in the first battle. Jin met his gaze without responding.
"Jin Gyeong and the Vamel Alliance have fought enough for us. I cannot express my gratitude in words... But Jin Gyeong, at this rate, you and your people will also be swept away by Zipfel's flames."
"Shuras, I am a Runcandel. Runcandels and Zipfel are meant to kill each other."

"That's not a reason for you to die in this land, Jin Gyeong. Don't you have a future, Jin Gyeong? Instead of fighting and dying with us here, isn't it better to plan for the future? When midnight passes and dawn comes, the enemies will attack."
"I won't die in this land, Shuras. And the talk about planning for the future... It applies to the knights of Hairan as well."

"No, it's different. We have no future. You might have plans to evacuate us and incorporate us into the Vamel Alliance or Runcandel for safety. But if we do that, we will be crushed by the guilt of abandoning Hairan for the rest of our lives."
In English, the passage translates to:
As Jin was choosing his words, Shuras focused his gaze on Dante's seal and followed up his previous statement.

"Jin, to be honest, we are worthless. Power, wisdom, wealth, influence within the empire. All are trivially small. In this war, the role of most of the knights gathered for Hairan is like a bird's blood."

"Ah, why do you say that? Huh? Thanks to you guys, refugees were saved, Dante got courage, and if the numbers are small in such a war, it doesn't look good. You guys were cool, weren't you? Why do you belittle yourself?"
"When the Black Dragon says so, I don't know what to do. But even considering all that, we are insignificant in this war."
"Oh, so you're going to sit still and die because it doesn't matter if you die?"

"We can hurt the enemy by dying on this land. The Zipfel and the Empire, trampling on the petty knights who vowed to protect the gods and fought till the end... The enemies will lose their honor by killing us. Jin, aren't you the one who often humiliates their honor?"
"I've never sacrificed my life to humiliate the enemy's honor."

"You haven't thrown it away, but you've always risked it. We're just risking our lives too. To disgrace their honor. This is the most meaningful counterattack that ordinary knights like us can make against the great powers."
Looking coldly as Shuras put it, he was not wrong.
Jin also knew this himself. His attempt to save the knights gathered for Hairan was simply because he did not want to see them die.
"If you keep coming out like this, I'll save you forcibly."
"Sir."
Shuras bowed his head as he held Jin's hand.
"Sir Jin... Please respect us. As a fellow warrior, as a comrade who fought together."
"Don't you think it's too much, Sir Shuras. It's almost like telling me to watch you guys die."
"That's because there's nowhere else to say respect us but you. I'm sorry, we're just such bad people who waste your grace."
Shuras held Jin's hand for a while, then turned around and walked out of the war room.
"Murakan."
"Yeah."
"Before midnight tonight, make all the knights except for the direct line of Hairan faint and transport them to Tikan with Valkas, the Proch siblings."
"All of them?"
All of them, just as he was about to answer that.
Quikantel sighed as he grabbed Jin's shoulder.
"Lord Quikantel."

"That Shuras guy, although he says that... He went around all night convincing all the families gathered for Hairan. He said that their holding on was too cruel to you, and that only the old knights including himself should stay and the rest should leave to lighten the load."
"Hoo."
"It seemed like an action made not because they want to survive, but because they know it's the best decision for you. And I even felt his painful inner feelings."
"No matter what, too many lives are at stake. Is it a joke or a fart for our kid to just let them die?"
"...Also, the knights have not yet given up hope on Ron. Apparently, imagining the sight of themselves not being there when Ron wakes up is more terrifying than death."
The fact that the knights are prepared for death and not leaving the castle is undeniably painful for Jin.
However, for the knights, it was a matter of existential significance.
"That's why I think it might be better to respect them. Jin, it's painful for you too, but for them, it's a matter tied to the very essence of their existence."
For a long time, Jin couldn't take his eyes off the door that Shuras had left through.
